Mr. President,
Distinguished delegates,
At the outset, I would like to congratulate H.E. Dennis Francis on his
election as President of the 78" session of the UN General Assembly. | am
confident that with his wealth ofexperience and excellent cap ability, he will help
ensure the success of this session.
I also wish to voice my appreciationfor the significant contributions of
H.E. Csaba K6rési, President of the 77" session of the UN General Assembly,
and H.E. Antonio Guterres, Secretary General of the UN.
Mr. President,
Distinguished delegates,
Having endured great
sufferings,
sacrifices and losses from wars,
separation, embargo ofthe past century, VietNam understands better than anyone
and appreciates profoundly the value ofpeace, cooperation, and development.
With perseverance and tireless efforts in the spirit of “putting the past
behind, overcoming differences, harnessing similarities, and striving towards
thefuture” to turn enemies into friends, confrontation into dialogue, and through
contending and cooperating, turn adversaries into partners.
By doing that, Viet Nam is recognized by international friends as a model
for
post-war cooperation,
recovery and
reconciliation
for
the common
development and prosperity of all parties concerned.
To this end, it would be remiss not to mention the three most important and
decisive factors in international cooperation - trust, sincerity and solidarity.
Trust helps erase animosity and bridge differences, and is the prerequisite
for solid, effective and substantive ties.
Sincerity
brings
sympathy,
reinforces
hope,
trust and
solidarity
domestically, which makes up the strength ofa State, a nation and all ofits people.
Solidarity internationally enhances multilateralism and creates global
strength.
This is also the spirit thatwe wish to underscore and promote at this year’s
session. Only by building upon trust, sincerity andsolidarity around the world,
strengthening of the UN’s role and mobilizing the active participation of all

and stability prevails at the macro level, hostilities, conflicts and tension remain
at the micro one. In addition, arms races and increasing risks from weapons of
mass destruction loom large. The consequences ofCOVID-19 continue to persist,
while the global economy records slow and unequal recovery, with high inflation
and growing risks.
At the same time, non-traditional security challenges, natural disasters,
climate change, environmental issues, food, energy, water, and cyber security are
evolving in
a complex and unpredictable manner.
In addition, our world today is facing four critical crises.
First, there is the crisis oftrust amid the most intense geopolitical tensions
since the Cold War.
Second, there is the crisis ofmultilateral cooperation due to fragmentation
and division.
Third, there is the crisis of legal
principles reflected through the
undermining of international law and the UN Charter in certain corners.
And fourth, there is the crisis ofresources to respond to global issues, such
as poverty eradication, education, health, humanitarian assistance, diseases,
natural disasters, and climate change.
Against this backdrop, the critical questionis: As leadersofthe world, what
do we need to do to help our respective nation and the world as a whole
overcome current obstacles?
The answer, in my opinion, is: We need to jointly build trust, showcase
sincerity, bolster solidarity, enhance bilateral and multilateral cooperation,
effectively respond to global and whole-of-population challenges, promote
sustainable development
with thepeople as the centre, the actor, the goal, the
driver and the resourcefor growth.
Iam ofthe view that global challenges require globalsolutions. In addition,
as these issues affect each and every person, we should adopt a whole-of-
population, comprehensive and holistic approach.
In this spirit,
I would like to outline five clusters ofsolutions asfollows:
First, it is necessary to buildupon sincerity, reinforce strategic trust and
call upon countries to uphold responsibility as the basis for our efforts.
Sincerity and trust are fostered and bolstered through candid dialogue, on
the basis of mutual respect, shared interests and joint efforts to address
differences, as well as the prevention and containment of conflicts.

Second, a global solution is to enhance international solidarity and
cooperation. Fach country needs to place their interests in the broader picture of
the international community’s interests, and join hands to protect and promote
multilateralism, and enhance the central role of the UN.
This can be achieved through new and more robust multilateral initiatives
and actions, for the interests ofall countries and peoples. It is also necessary to
support the UN Secretary General’s SDG Stimulus via vigorous, concrete,
practical and effective commitments and actions.
Let us pursue unity instead ofdivision, dialogue instead ofconfrontation,
and cooperation instead ofisolation and divergence.
Once again, Viet Nam affirms its solidarity with other countries, including
Cuba, and urges the United States to put an end to its embargo against Cuba.
Third, a whole-of-population solution is topromotepolicies that identify
the people as the centre, the goal, the actor, the driver, and the resource of
sustainable development, while ensuring that no one is left behind.
Development can only be truly meaningful when it brings about practical
benefits to each and every person, particularly in such prioritized areas as
investment in promoting education, creating jobs, ensuring social security,
providing healthcare, improving resilience and adaptation, and preventing natural
disasters and diseases.
Fourth, it is necessary to implement holistic political, economic and
social measures to ensure security and stability. We need to develop and
transition into a green, digital, circular, sharing and smart economy, promote
innovations and start-ups, reduce trade and investment barriers, facilitate market
access and conclude more FTAs.
It is also necessary to expedite the reforms of international institutions,
particularly financial and monetary ones, towards greater equity and equality for
developing countries, and improve their capacity to effectively manage risks.
Fifth, we need to mobilize and effectively utilize resources, in which self-
reliance,
resilience,
and the effective harnessing of our potentials and
advantages are imp ortant factors underlying the success, prosperity and strength
of each nation, region and the world at large.
Developing countries, particularly least developed countries, are currently
most vulnerable to the severe consequences ofclimate change, natural disasters,
and diseases. They need to receive substantive and effective assistance in terms
of finance, technology, human resource development and governance of
coordination.

President Ho Chi Minh, the beloved great leader of Viet Nam’s people,
National liberation hero and Greatman ofculture once said: “A country is rooted
in its people. Only when the root holdsstrong can the tree standfirm. We shall
build the fort of victory on the foundation of our people’s efforts” and
“Solidarity, solidarity, great solidarity. Success, success, great success.”
By building upon this philosophy, Viet Nam has recorded important and
historic achievements after nearly 40 years of Doi Moi across the board,
particularly in terms of socio-economic development and improvement of the
people’s living standards. The multidimensional poverty rate in Viet Nam has
dropped to under 2%.
Viet Nam
steadfastly pursues
the
consistent
foreign
policy
of
independence, self-reliance, multilateralization and diversification of external
relations, and remain a friend, a reliable partner, and an active, responsible
member ofthe international community, forpeace, cooperation, development, and
prosperity of all countries worldwide.
Viet Nam will continue to be a reliable and responsible partner of the
international community. Vietnamese men and women from the People’s Army
and Police forces have been participating in the UN peacekeeping missions,
conveyinga strong message ofpeace, friendship, cooperation and delopment.
We are also expediting energy transition to achieve net-zero emissions by
2050. In addition, VietNammaintain food security for
a population of 100 million
people, while striving to export around 7 million tons of rice this year,
contributing to ensuring global food security.
[On this occasion, I would like to announce Viet Nam’s National
Commitment towards SDG transition.]
Mr. President,
Distinguished delegates,
Froma region plagued withwar and division, Southeast Asia has emerged
as a region ofsolidarity, friendship and cooperation, and an epicentrumofgrowth.
Moreover,ASEAN has affirmed its centrality in maintaining peace, security and
prosperity in the region.
We wish to reaffirm our commitment to working with countries within and
outside the region to safeguard peace, stability, security, safety, and freedom of
navigation in the South China Sea in accordance with international law and the
1982 UNCLOS.

uncharted seas ofpeace, stability, cooperation, and development.
Thus, let us be responsible sailors, stand united, uphold trust and act in
unison to “steady our helm” and take the “UNvessel” to new horizons ofgreater
and more inclusive prosperity.
